date: # Fed balance-sheet programmes (and the Treasury's own buybacks): start
name: what was bought.
QE1
what: $1.75tn of agency debt, MBS and (from March 2009) Treasuries.

name: Operation Twist
what: Sold short Treasuries to buy long ones: lengthened the Fed's holdings without growing them.

name: QE3
what: Open-ended: $40bn a month of MBS, plus $45bn of Treasuries from 2013; tapered through 2014.

name: QT1
what: Let maturing bonds roll off, up to $50bn a month.

name: Reserve management bills
what: $60bn a month of Treasury bills after the repo spike: technically not QE.

name: Covid QE
what: Unlimited at first; about $4.6tn of Treasuries and MBS in two years.

name: QT2
what: Runoff up to $95bn a month, slowed in 2024 and 2025, ended 1 December 2025.

name: Reserve management purchases
what: Treasury bill purchases to keep reserves ample after QT ended.
note: from memory: verify the start date and pace

name: Treasury buybacks
what: The Treasury (not the Fed) buys back older, less-traded bonds for liquidity support and cash management, funded by new issues.
